title: Знакомство с сыном Елены  (Meeting Elena's Son)

segments.t: Hearing a scuffle in the hallway, Elena Pavlovna rushes out in her robe and stops Chef Barinov from twisting the intruder's arm, revealing that the young man is her son Vasily. Barinov points out that Vasily smells of alcohol, sparking an argument between mother and son.
Нет, ты давай, иди в комнату.
Фу ты елки, Виктор Петрович, мой…
И что вы с ним здесь?
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'What on earth is going on here?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'is going on'.
Нет, ты давай, иди в комнату.
'No, go on into your room right now.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'there is no' and finishing on 'the room'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Viktor Petrovich, stop right there.' The meaning hinges on 'Viktor' working together with 'to stop' in spoken Russian.
Фу ты елки, Виктор Петрович, мой…
'Good grief, Viktor Petrovich, this is my...' Vika anchors the line on 'ugh', while 'my' completes the thought.
'I get it, you do not need to finish that sentence.' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'to continue'. Vika answers right away.
И что вы с ним здесь?
'Wait, what are you doing here with him?' The grammar packs 'both' and 'here' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Alright, stop that right now, please.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'like this' and finishing on 'there you go'.
'And besides, why are you even here?' In Russian, the idea of 'both' flows naturally into 'here' without extra filler words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'By the way, he smells like alcohol.' The meaning hinges on 'from' working together with 'it smells' in spoken Russian.
'Mom, please do not even start.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Mum' before landing on 'start'.
'Maybe you really would be better off in the army.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'of course' and finishing on 'army'. Vika answers right away.
'Go to your room.' In Russian, the idea of 'go' flows naturally into 'the room' without extra filler words.
'No, did you see that?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'there is no' and finishing on 'saw'. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Нет, ты давай, иди в комнату.
Фу ты елки, Виктор Петрович, мой…
И что вы с ним здесь?
That wraps up this scene as elena Pavlovna rushes out of the bathroom to stop Chef Barinov from twisting the arm of her son Vasily, who rudely criticizes their relationship. Until next time!
